name: Rachel
description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: When Jacob saw Rachel he rolled the stone from the well's mouth and watered the flock, flexing like a bird puffing its chest, did she see me? Right away it altered his behavior. Abram and Isaac got married and went about God's business; Jacob lost his mind over Rachel. The kiss was a greeting, like the Northern Kingdom's kiss on the cheek, not making out.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Leah was tender eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured, and Jacob loved Rachel. He had already run to roll the stone from the well's mouth, watered her flock, and kissed her when she came out with the sheep; his eyes were fixed on her from the start.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

points: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her. And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her. And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. See that — they made a wedding feast.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Leah was tender eyed, but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured, and Jacob loved Rachel and served seven years that seemed but a few days for the love he had to her. Contrast Isaac: married, then loved. Jacob's love was based on physical beauty, emotional attraction, and romantic motivation, and what followed was deception, competition between Leah, Rachel, and the handmaids, and family tension. Scripture does not hide the cost of romance-driven decisions; it documents it.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed unto him but a few days for the love he had to her. That is how fine she was to him: with six and a half years still left, it felt like a couple of days.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

points: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah and served with Laban yet seven other years. When the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren. Jacob was showing more favor to Rachel because he was more attracted to Rachel.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

points: Rachel was favoured and beautiful, and beautiful women have issues and use their beauty to control brothers; she envied her sister and was depressed because she had no children.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: When Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. Envy: that is Satan. And she said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die: give me a baby or I am going to kill myself. A very beautiful woman can be very manipulative and use her beauty to control you; Eve did that to Adam, and here the same thing is being done to Jacob. When a woman knows you love her more than God, she will try to use certain things against you. Brothers, never put a woman above your God: God comes first.

Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, envied her sister, and told Jacob, Give me children, or else I die. Jacob's anger was kindled against her: Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb? Jacob was not the problem; he was having no trouble producing children.

Their arguing is the trouble in the flesh the scriptures speak of. If thou marry, thou hast not sinned, but such shall have trouble in the flesh: it is not all going to be sweet all the time. Rachel's trouble in the flesh was that she envied her sister and could not bear children, and she took it out on Jacob.

note.label: Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire

points: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God's stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb? This is an argument Moses saw between Jacob and his wife, and he wrote it down in a kosher way for us. Jacob was angry, and when a man is angry he lifts his voice. That is not abuse. Sisters, when your husband gets angry and yells and corrects you, that is not abuse; take the correction, see what he is saying, and fix it, instead of trying to justify yourself. Because when a woman tries to justify herself, Satan comes in her mind saying, he was wrong for what he said to you, that is abuse right there; and if you listen to Satan, you end up divorced. A sister called the teacher this same week saying her husband was abusive; when she explained, it was arguments, and some things the brother should not have said, but it was still not abuse. Abuse is abuse, and correction is not it.

Reuben found mandrakes in the field in the days of wheat harvest and brought them unto his mother Leah. Rachel asked for them, and Leah answered, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband? and wouldest thou take away my son's mandrakes also? So Rachel granted, He shall lie with thee to night for thy son's mandrakes.

note.label: Genesis 30: Trouble in the Flesh and a Righteous Hire

points: Laban went to shear his sheep, and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's. Remember what we read in Proverbs about beauty: yes, she was fine, but she was a thief. She might have been a fine thief, but she was a thief.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

points: Jacob answered that he went away because he was afraid Laban would take his daughters from him by force, and said, With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

points: Rachel travailed, had hard labour, and died: the seriousness of birth is understood; his own wife's four pregnancies were high risk, the doctors pressed for an abortion of the last child over an abnormality, and the answer was to trust the Lord.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: Rachel travailed in hard labour and died bearing her second son; she called him Benoni, but his father called him Benjamin, the son of the right hand. He was the twelfth son, and Jacob set a pillar upon Rachel's grave in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

points: Jacob told Joseph where his mother was buried: Rachel died by him in the land of Canaan in the way of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and he buried her there.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: All the people that were in the gate and the elders said, We are witnesses. They blessed the marriage: the Lord make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel; and let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah, of the seed which the Lord shall give thee of this young woman.

A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted because they were not; but the Most High tells her to refrain her voice from weeping, for her work shall be rewarded and her children shall come again from the land of the enemy to their own border.

cases.name: Rachel and the stolen teraphim
cases.charge: Stealing her father’s images, and hiding them under her while she sat upon them
cases.preview: Rachel stole the images that were her father’s, hid them in the camel’s furniture and sat upon them, and told her father she could not rise up before him, so he searched and found them not.
